**Explicit Supporting Facts (as found in the page text)**  

- Ngugi wa Thiong’o has written “more than three dozen books, plays, poetry and essays that have been translated into more than 30 languages.”  
  *“His more than three dozen books, plays, poetry and essays have been translated into more than 30 languages.”*

- His 1967 novel *A Grain of Wheat* was highlighted by former U.S. President Barack Obama on his 2018 summer reading list.  
  *“...Ngugi's 1967 novel A Grain of Wheat (Heinemann, 1967), set in the wake of the Mau Mau uprising, on his summer reading list...”*

- In 1977 Ngugi was arrested for writing in Gikuyu and was imprisoned at a maximum‑security prison in Nairobi.  
  *“In 1977, he co‑authored… which was written in Gikuyu and performed… The African‑run Kenyan government stopped the play and arrested Ngugi… He was imprisoned at a maximum‑security prison in Nairobi.”*

- Ngugi was released from prison and subsequently left Kenya due to threats of violence, ultimately settling in London before taking positions at Yale, NYU, and UCI.  
  *“After his release from prison, Ngugi left his country amid threats of violence and death. He settled in London for a time before taking a position at Yale in 1989… Then came an invitation from UCI…”*

- Ngugi founded and directs the International Center for Writing and Translation at the University of California, Irvine.  
  *“...founding director of the UCI’s International Center for Writing and Translation…”*
